headline: Learned representations predict mutation, metabolite, and protein interaction outcomes
label: Multimodal Biomedical Data Integration
summary: Self-supervised and deep learning models now draw on ~50,000 tumors, MS/MS spectra, and deep mutational scans, pointing toward scalable multimodal integration.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations that map heterogeneous biomedical measurements into predictive spaces, though not every item shares it. MMRL learns self-supervised representations of somatic missense mutations from ~50,000 tumors and outperforms TMB for prognosis. DEEPNET-LLM restricts de novo metabolite structure prediction from MS/MS spectra to molecular-community neighborhoods. A random forest combines MINT embeddings with condition-specific mass-spec abundance to predict differential protein-protein interactions across eight cell types. MaskNGly applies protein language model embeddings zero-shot to N-glycosylation sites, while ESMRank and MIL-BC learn from deep mutational scans and domain bags respectively. The MET kinase benchmark finds deep learning models largely ligand-invariant. What is new is combining distinct views, including sequence embeddings, spectra, interaction networks, and mutational scans, benchmarked against TMB, ProteinGym, and a sequence baseline.
